title: Everyday Leadership Techniques
body: Run a short huddle and follow up on one standard.
notes: Open with a club event about to start.
aria: Everyday Leadership Techniques. Run a short huddle and follow up on one standard.

title: Techniques
body: Part IV uses Chapters 18, 19 and 20 and the official huddle and conversation tools.
notes: Keep tool names separate from chapter titles.
aria: Techniques. Part IV uses Chapters 18, 19 and 20 and the official huddle and conversation tools.

title: From huddle to follow-up
body: Trace one standard through a week.
notes: Use the same event throughout the worked example.
aria: From huddle to follow-up. Trace one standard through a week.

title: Four parts of a huddle
body: Set the tone, name one priority, recognize an action and invite input within five minutes.
notes: Allow time to respond after the brief opening. [BRENEN MAP] Official theme from the published site/templates, but no chapter number/title is confirmed. Brenen will map this lesson to the actual chapter before the paid version ships. Do not invent a title.
aria: Four parts of a huddle. Set the tone, name one priority, recognize an action and invite input within five minutes.

title: Why one priority?
body: A list of five priorities leaves a new volunteer unsure where to start.
notes: Reduce a five-item speech to one decision.
aria: Why one priority?. A list of five priorities leaves a new volunteer unsure where to start.

title: Recognition a person can repeat
body: Name who did what and why it mattered.
notes: Use recent work that actually happened.
aria: Recognition a person can repeat. Name who did what and why it mattered.

title: Activity: write four huddle lines
body: Draft tone, priority, recognition and an invitation.
notes: Practice saying the four lines aloud.
aria: Activity: write four huddle lines. Draft tone, priority, recognition and an invitation.

title: Screen recording: run the huddle
body: Plan a 5–7 minute contrast between a focused huddle and a scattered one.
notes: Supply two scripts and mark the change. [BRENEN MAP] Official theme from the published site/templates, but no chapter number/title is confirmed. Brenen will map this lesson to the actual chapter before the paid version ships. Do not invent a title.
aria: Screen recording: run the huddle. Plan a 5–7 minute contrast between a focused huddle and a scattered one.

title: The affirmation rhythm
body: Chapter 20 describes roughly 80% affirmation and 20% correction.
notes: Keep praise earned rather than counting empty compliments. [BRENEN EXCERPT: 2–4 sentences from the mapped chapter, approved by Brenen]
aria: The affirmation rhythm. Chapter 20 describes roughly 80% affirmation and 20% correction.

title: Why notice good work?
body: Specific recognition helps people see what to repeat.
notes: Contrast with only speaking up after a mistake.
aria: Why notice good work?. Specific recognition helps people see what to repeat.

title: Activity: three affirmations
body: List three observed actions and one issue to discuss privately.
notes: Use roles on the local worksheet.
aria: Activity: three affirmations. List three observed actions and one issue to discuss privately.

title: Look up every eight to ten minutes
body: Check for work worth noticing during the shift or meeting.
notes: Adapt the Leadership Rhythm toolkit. [BRENEN MAP] Official theme from the published site/templates, but no chapter number/title is confirmed. Brenen will map this lesson to the actual chapter before the paid version ships. Do not invent a title.
aria: Look up every eight to ten minutes. Check for work worth noticing during the shift or meeting.

title: Activity: choose a cue
body: Set a personal reminder appropriate for your setting.
notes: No tracking feature is needed.
aria: Activity: choose a cue. Set a personal reminder appropriate for your setting.

title: Private one-on-ones
body: Chapter 18 places an individual correction away from an audience.
notes: Choose a safe, appropriate place. [BRENEN EXCERPT: 2–4 sentences from the mapped chapter, approved by Brenen]
aria: Private one-on-ones. Chapter 18 places an individual correction away from an audience.

title: Ten minutes with a teammate
body: Open with an observation, listen and agree on a next action.
notes: Make it appropriate for peers.
aria: Ten minutes with a teammate. Open with an observation, listen and agree on a next action.

title: Write down what matters
body: Chapter 19 emphasizes factual documentation of an important correction.
notes: Preserve what was asked and agreed. [BRENEN EXCERPT: 2–4 sentences from the mapped chapter, approved by Brenen]
aria: Write down what matters. Chapter 19 emphasizes factual documentation of an important correction.

title: A useful note
body: Write the date, fact, expectation and agreement under the applicable process.
notes: Do not build a public record of someone else's mistakes.
aria: A useful note. Write the date, fact, expectation and agreement under the applicable process.

title: Following up
body: Choose when you will check the agreed standard again.
notes: Show what happens when nobody checks. [BRENEN MAP] Official theme from the published site/templates, but no chapter number/title is confirmed. Brenen will map this lesson to the actual chapter before the paid version ships. Do not invent a title.
aria: Following up. Choose when you will check the agreed standard again.

title: Mid-quiz: three decisions
body: Check the one priority, the meaning of 80/20 and a private conversation.
notes: Explain the tradeoff in each scene.
aria: Mid-quiz: three decisions. Check the one priority, the meaning of 80/20 and a private conversation.

title: When a conversation is needed
body: A repeated missed handoff deserves a factual, private discussion.
notes: Use the official five-step guide as the source. [BRENEN MAP] Official theme from the published site/templates, but no chapter number/title is confirmed. Brenen will map this lesson to the actual chapter before the paid version ships. Do not invent a title.
aria: When a conversation is needed. A repeated missed handoff deserves a factual, private discussion.

title: Choose the setting
body: Find a calm, appropriate private time.
notes: Students should involve a trusted adult for harassment, discrimination, violence or safety issues. [BRENEN MAP] Official theme from the published site/templates, but no chapter number/title is confirmed. Brenen will map this lesson to the actual chapter before the paid version ships. Do not invent a title.
aria: Choose the setting. Find a calm, appropriate private time.

title: Lead with facts
body: Describe the last two missed start times and the effect on setup.
notes: Remove guesses about attitude. [BRENEN MAP] Official theme from the published site/templates, but no chapter number/title is confirmed. Brenen will map this lesson to the actual chapter before the paid version ships. Do not invent a title.
aria: Lead with facts. Describe the last two missed start times and the effect on setup.

title: State the expectation
body: Say what needs to happen, when and how the person can respond.
notes: Use a commitment within the student's role. [BRENEN MAP] Official theme from the published site/templates, but no chapter number/title is confirmed. Brenen will map this lesson to the actual chapter before the paid version ships. Do not invent a title.
aria: State the expectation. Say what needs to happen, when and how the person can respond.

title: Listen for an obstacle
body: Ask what is getting in the way, then listen before proposing a fix.
notes: Use a scheduling conflict as an example. [BRENEN MAP] Official theme from the published site/templates, but no chapter number/title is confirmed. Brenen will map this lesson to the actual chapter before the paid version ships. Do not invent a title.
aria: Listen for an obstacle. Ask what is getting in the way, then listen before proposing a fix.

title: Explain the real consequence
body: Describe the next step you actually control, such as involving the advisor.
notes: Avoid threats or pretending a club officer can fire classmates. [BRENEN MAP] Official theme from the published site/templates, but no chapter number/title is confirmed. Brenen will map this lesson to the actual chapter before the paid version ships. Do not invent a title.
aria: Explain the real consequence. Describe the next step you actually control, such as involving the advisor.

title: Check your purpose
body: Aim to help, describe behavior, use facts and offer a path forward.
notes: Review the tone of the first sentence. [BRENEN MAP] Official theme from the published site/templates, but no chapter number/title is confirmed. Brenen will map this lesson to the actual chapter before the paid version ships. Do not invent a title.
aria: Check your purpose. Aim to help, describe behavior, use facts and offer a path forward.

title: Two versions of the conversation
body: Compare a private factual opening with a shaming group message.
notes: Annotate the changes one sentence at a time.
aria: Two versions of the conversation. Compare a private factual opening with a shaming group message.

title: Activity: draft a five-step script
body: Choose a late setup volunteer or a missed project handoff.
notes: Include the other person's reply.
aria: Activity: draft a five-step script. Choose a late setup volunteer or a missed project handoff.

title: Screen recording: difficult conversation
body: Plan an 8–12 minute role-play and a one-minute debrief.
notes: Required before paid release. Use a written dialogue first. [BRENEN MAP] Official theme from the published site/templates, but no chapter number/title is confirmed. Brenen will map this lesson to the actual chapter before the paid version ships. Do not invent a title.
aria: Screen recording: difficult conversation. Plan an 8–12 minute role-play and a one-minute debrief.

title: Hold the important details
body: Keep the handoff check on a short-staffed day.
notes: Distinguish quality from personal taste. [BRENEN MAP] Official theme from the published site/templates, but no chapter number/title is confirmed. Brenen will map this lesson to the actual chapter before the paid version ships. Do not invent a title.
aria: Hold the important details. Keep the handoff check on a short-staffed day.

title: A weekly sequence
body: Huddle, observe, affirm, address a miss privately, write the agreement and follow up.
notes: Have the learner put the steps in order.
aria: A weekly sequence. Huddle, observe, affirm, address a miss privately, write the agreement and follow up.

title: A truthful huddle bullet
body: Describe the huddle you actually ran and what the group did next.
notes: Skip the claim if the student only practiced.
aria: A truthful huddle bullet. Describe the huddle you actually ran and what the group did next.

title: Worksheet: My Techniques Card
body: Include the four-part script, observation log, conversation draft and follow-up.
notes: Keep notes about peers off the server.
aria: Worksheet: My Techniques Card. Include the four-part script, observation log, conversation draft and follow-up.

title: Common traps
body: Spot vague praise, public correction, revenge notes and the speech disguised as a huddle.
notes: Rewrite one line.
aria: Common traps. Spot vague praise, public correction, revenge notes and the speech disguised as a huddle.

title: What the techniques have in common
body: Review Chapters 18–20 alongside the one-priority huddle.
notes: Tie each technique to a concrete action.
aria: What the techniques have in common. Review Chapters 18–20 alongside the one-priority huddle.

title: Next: a team that has drifted
body: Introduce the longer process of rebuilding a routine.
notes: Point to L5.
aria: Next: a team that has drifted. Introduce the longer process of rebuilding a routine.

title: Optional completion line
body: Preview a record or a skill actually practiced.
notes: Keep a mock conversation off the experience list.
aria: Optional completion line. Preview a record or a skill actually practiced.

title: End question: 80/20
body: Select a pattern of genuine affirmation and targeted correction.
notes: Reject a rigid praise quota.
aria: End question: 80/20. Select a pattern of genuine affirmation and targeted correction.

title: End question: a private correction
body: Choose a setting consistent with Chapter 18.
notes: Address safety and standing.
aria: End question: a private correction. Choose a setting consistent with Chapter 18.

title: End question: a factual opening
body: Find the sentence with an observation and an impact.
notes: Avoid labels about personality.
aria: End question: a factual opening. Find the sentence with an observation and an impact.

title: End question: a written record
body: Choose a short factual follow-up note using Chapter 19.
notes: Leave out gossip.
aria: End question: a written record. Choose a short factual follow-up note using Chapter 19.

title: End question: a useful huddle
body: Choose a single priority that helps people decide what comes first.
notes: Give a reason for the best choice.
aria: End question: a useful huddle. Choose a single priority that helps people decide what comes first.

title: Answer review
body: Explain choices and invite another attempt.
notes: Four of five completes the future class.
aria: Answer review. Explain choices and invite another attempt.

title: Use the card this week
body: Run one huddle and offer one private affirmation or correction within your role.
notes: Record when you will check back.
aria: Use the card this week. Run one huddle and offer one private affirmation or correction within your role.
